title: Keeping a record of what your shop did
target: Where Supermarket Simulator writes things down for you, so you can check orders, money and warnings instead of trying to remember them.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that has taken at least one order
At least one bill that comes due
The computer or tablet within reach

steps.do: Let the notebook hold your orders rather than trying to remember them.
steps.because: orders are kept in a notebook and a container of its own, with a display of its own (OrderNotebook, OrderNotebookContainer, OrderNotebookDisplay)

steps.do: Go to the money window for loans, bills and growth instead of hunting through menus.
steps.because: those screens are built on a window made of tabs, with a tab each for loans, bills and growth (BaseWindow, WindowTab, LoansTab, BillsTab, GrowthTab)

steps.do: Open the loan payments tab when the question is a repayment rather than a loan.
steps.because: a loan has a payments tab of its own beside it (LoanPaymentsTab)

steps.do: Look for licences and storage in the same arrangement.
steps.because: licences and storage sit in the same window of tabs (LicensesTab, StorageTab)

steps.do: Read warnings as their own system rather than as more popups.
steps.because: warnings are run by a system of their own and kept in a pool (WarningSystem, WarningsPool)

steps.do: Match the warning to what is actually happening before you act on it.
steps.because: warnings are sorted into kinds, with an interaction warning type and a baker warning type among them (InteractionWarningType, BakerWarningType)

steps.do: Check on a delayed warning rather than assuming nothing happened.
steps.because: a warning can be stopped as well as started, with a delay routine of its own (StopWarning, WarningDelayCoroutine)

commonMistakes: Tracking orders in your head when the game writes them into a notebook.
Looking for a bill under the loan's own screen instead of the payments tab.
Treating a warning as decoration rather than as something that tells you what to do next.
Assuming a warning that has stopped means the problem is gone.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
